test_title: SSC CGL 2024 Tier-I Official Paper (Held On: 25 Sept, 2024 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: In a quadrilateral ABCD, AB = BC, AD = DC. ∠ABD = 68º, ∠ADB = (2y-7)º, ∠BDC = 33º, ∠DBC = (3x+2)º. Then the value of 2x+3y is:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

A quadrilateral with two distinct pairs of equal adjacent sides is a kite.

The main diagonal of a kite bisects the opposite interior angles.

⇒ ∠ABD = ∠DBC ⇒ 68 = 3x + 2 ⇒ x = 22

⇒ ∠ADB = ∠BDC ⇒ 2y − 7 = 33 ⇒ y = 20

⇒ 2x + 3y = 2 × 22 + 3 × 20 = 44 + 60 = 104

**∴ The correct answer is 104.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

In quadrilateral ABCD:

⇒ AB = BC

⇒ AD = DC

⇒ ∠ABD = 68º

⇒ ∠ADB = (2y−7)º

⇒ ∠BDC = 33º

⇒ ∠DBC = (3x+2)º

**Method:**

Since the adjacent sides are equal, ABCD is a kite. The diagonal BD divides the kite into two congruent triangles, ΔABD and ΔCBD.

In ΔABD and ΔCBD:

⇒ AB = CB (Given)

⇒ AD = CD (Given)

⇒ BD = BD (Common Side)

⇒ By SSS congruence criterion, ΔABD ≅ ΔCBD.

Corresponding angles of congruent triangles are equal (CPCT):

⇒ ∠ABD = ∠CBD

⇒ 68 = 3x + 2

⇒ 3x = 66 ⇒ x = 22

Also,

⇒ ∠ADB = ∠CDB

⇒ 2y − 7 = 33

⇒ 2y = 40 ⇒ y = 20

Now, calculate the value of 2x + 3y:

⇒ 2x + 3y = 2 × 22 + 3 × 20

⇒ 44 + 60 = 104

**∴ The correct answer is 104.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Properties of a Kite

A kite is a quadrilateral with two distinct pairs of equal-length sides that are adjacent to each other. Its diagonals intersect at right angles (90º).

Congruence in Kite

The main diagonal (connecting the vertices where the equal sides meet) divides the kite into two congruent triangles via the SSS rule.

Area of a Kite

The area of a kite is half the product of the lengths of its diagonals: Area = ½ × d₁ × d₂.
